sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Strong breadth is concentrated in defensive and financial sectors as four groups achieve all-green status, while Utilities suffer a sharp decline and Consumer Cyclical remains anchored at the bottom.

Energy continues to lead the market with the highest overall momentum score of 0.80 (ranking #1 YTD), but broader market strength is consolidating in a cluster of defensive and value-oriented sectors. Financials (0.72 momentum), Healthcare (0.62), Real Estate (0.62), and Consumer Defensive (0.57) are all exhibiting "all-green" breadth, indicating positive performance across the week, month, quarter, half-year, and YTD. Each of these four sectors, along with Basic Materials, improved its rank by +1 spot over the last five sessions, pointing to a steady rotation into these areas.

Conversely, Utilities experienced a severe drop, falling -4 spots to rank 9 with a weak momentum score of 0.23. Industrials also ticked down -1 spot to rank 4 (0.35 momentum). Consumer Cyclical remains the weakest sector in the market, sitting at the bottom of the momentum rankings at 0.22 (rank 11 YTD), closely followed by Communication Services at 0.25.

## Strength
* **Robust Breadth:** 4 of 11 sectors are "all-green" (positive across all timeframes), led by Financials (0.72 momentum) and Healthcare (0.62 momentum).
* **Defensive Support:** Real Estate (0.62 momentum) and Consumer Defensive (0.57 momentum) round out the all-green list, showing consistent gains across short and long horizons.
* **Energy Dominance:** Energy holds the absolute highest momentum score at 0.80, maintaining its position as the #1 YTD rank.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Broad Upward Rotation:** Five sectors improved their rank by +1 spot over the last 5 sessions: Real Estate (rank 3), Basic Materials (rank 5), Consumer Defensive (rank 6), Financials (rank 7), and Healthcare (rank 8).
* **Utilities Collapse:** Utilities fell a sharp -4 spots in rank over the past 5 sessions, dropping to rank 9 with a weak momentum score of 0.23.
* **Persistent Laggards:** Consumer Cyclical (0.22 momentum, rank 11) and Communication Services (0.25 momentum, rank 10) remain stuck at the bottom of the momentum table.

## Divergences
* **Stable All-Green Base:** There are no fragile all-green sectors identified, indicating that the positive momentum in Financials, Healthcare, Real Estate, and Consumer Defensive remains structurally supported.
* **No Active Divergences:** Early-warning indicators show no active rank-momentum mismatches or fragile performance trends across the 11 groups.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Market breadth remains stable with 25% of industry groups in "all-green" territory, led by dominant energy and steel sectors, while a sharp short-term rotation favors consumer cyclicals like Luxury Goods at the expense of building and industrial materials.

Heavy industry and cyclicals continue to anchor long-term market strength. Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.925 momentum) and Steel (0.889 momentum) maintain their sustained leadership alongside Consumer Electronics and Staffing & Employment Services. Meanwhile, a powerful weekly rotation has boosted consumer-facing and travel-related industries, with Luxury Goods jumping 25 spots to rank 53 and Education & Training Services climbing 21 spots to rank 70.

Conversely, defensive and heavy industrial sectors are fading rapidly. Building Products & Equipment shed 20 spots to fall to rank 61, and Aluminum fell 19 spots to rank 90. In terms of early-warning divergences, previously strong groups like REIT - Healthcare Facilities (momentum 0.67) are beginning to slip in rank, while low-momentum laggards like Medical Instruments & Supplies and Restaurants are starting to emerge.

## Strength
* **Solid Breadth:** 36 of 144 industry groups (25%) are in "all-green" territory, showing positive performance across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD timeframes.
* **Sustained Leaders:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.93) and Steel (momentum 0.89) lead the all-green cohort, alongside Consumer Electronics (momentum 0.88) and Staffing & Employment Services (momentum 0.87).
* **Financial & Retail Anchors:** Financial Conglomerates (momentum 0.82), REIT - Hotel & Motel (momentum 0.83), and Department Stores (momentum 0.81) represent strong, fully-aligned sectors.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Luxury Goods led weekly gains, climbing 25 spots to rank 53 (momentum 0.73), followed closely by Education & Training Services (+21 spots, rank 70) and Beverages - Wineries & Distilleries (+20 spots, rank 82).
* **Sharpest Decliners:** Building Products & Equipment plunged 20 spots to rank 61 (momentum 0.32), while Aluminum fell 19 spots to rank 90 (momentum 0.29) and Integrated Freight & Logistics dropped 18 spots to rank 49 (momentum 0.44).
* **Momentum Extremes:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing remains the top overall momentum leader (0.925, YTD rank 2), while Gambling (0.146, YTD rank 144) and Mortgage Finance (0.110, YTD rank 143) sit at the absolute bottom of the market.

## Divergences
* **Fading Strengths:** Several high-momentum groups are losing ground, notably REIT - Healthcare Facilities (momentum 0.67, down 9 spots) and Diagnostics & Research (momentum 0.62, down 8 spots).
* **Emerging Laggards:** Underperforming sectors are showing early signs of bottoming, with Medical Instruments & Supplies (+6 spots, momentum 0.35) and Restaurants (+6 spots, momentum 0.46) climbing in rank despite low overall momentum scores.
* **Defensive Slippage:** High-momentum transport and defensive groups are showing exhaustion, with Railroads (momentum 0.68) and Insurance - Reinsurance (momentum 0.67) both slipping 4 spots over the last 5 sessions.
